title: OneDrive and SharePoint: respond to access requests in the Share dialog
summary: Hold: the PowerShell reference does not establish that the sharing command implements the files-and-folders control shown beside it, and the audit command omits created requests despite the row promising them. The briefing also overstates uncertainty about external sharing restrictions, which Microsoft documents for SharePoint and OneDrive generally.

claims.claim: Only site admins and members of the site's Owners group can process the existing Access Requests list.
claims.quote: These issues occur because the affected users are not site admins (previously called site collection administrators) or members of the Owners group for the site. Only users with these specific permissions can process requests to the Access Requests list.

claims.claim: Disabling site access requests prevents non-members from requesting access.
claims.quote: You can prevent users who aren't members of the site from requesting access by turning off access requests.

claims.claim: The troubleshooting guidance requires a site collection administrator to enable access requests.
claims.quote: To resolve the errors, enable access requests for the affected site collection. You must be a site collection administrator to enable this feature.

claims.claim: The owners-only file, folder and site sharing option is at gear icon > Site permissions > Sharing settings > Change how members can share > Only site owners can share files, folders, and the site.
claims.quote:
In the site, select the gear icon, and then select **Site permissions**.
2. Under **Sharing settings**, select **Change how members can share**.
3. Select **Only site owners can share files, folders, and the site**.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -DisableSharingForNonOwners is the automation equivalent of restricting file and folder sharing to site owners.
claims.quote: Searched: "DisableSharingForNonOwners" "files" "folders"; "DisableSharingForNonOwners" "Only site owners". Read Set-SPOSite, including Example 4 and the parameter entry, and Limit sharing. The reference documents preventing invitations to the site, not this files-and-folders option.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to null rather than presenting this call as the equivalent of the file-and-folder sharing option. Remove the cmdlet-specific note and its corresponding explanation in Governance controls; retain the verified UI path.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference says DisableSharingForNonOwners prevents non-owners from inviting new users to the site.
claims.quote: This parameter prevents non-owners from inviting new users to the site.

claims.claim: The reference's exhaustive list of parameters valid for OneDrive sites excludes DisableSharingForNonOwners.
claims.quote: For OneDrive for Business site collection, the only valid parameters are Identity, AllowDownloadingNonWebViewableFiles, AllowEditing, ConditionalAccessPolicy, DefaultLinkPermission, DefaultSharingLinkType, DisableCompanyWideSharingLinks

In the site, select the gear icon, and then select **Site permissions**.
2. Under **Sharing settings**, select **Change how members can share**.

claims.claim: The printed Search-UnifiedAuditLog call searches created, accepted and denied access requests as the row describes.
claims.quote: The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation. The available values for this parameter depend on the RecordType value.
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <ExDateTime> -EndDate <ExDateTime> -Operations AccessRequestCreated,AccessRequestAccepted,AccessRequestDenied'. AccessRequestCreated is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-activities#sharing-and-access-request-activities; the current filter excludes it.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog runs in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is **Search-UnifiedAuditLog**.
